chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn ibn Urwah, the son of the sister of Shuayb Al-Aqarqufi, from his maternal uncle Shuayb, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is hungry, let him perform wudu and pray two rak'at, then say: O Lord, I am hungry, so feed me, for he will be fed from that moment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer and supplication for someone who is hungry and seeking food?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) outlines a concise ritual for seeking sustenance (rizq) involving ablution, a two-rak'ah prayer, and a direct supplication for food. It highlights the Shia emphasis on combining physical preparation with spiritual reliance, promising immediate provision as a sign of divine responsiveness to humble petition. This practice underscores the theological link between gratitude, ritual purity, and the tangible manifestation of God's mercy in daily life.

en.hubeali: Ali, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq, from Abdullah Bin Ahmad, from Al-Hassan Bin Urwat a son of the sister of Shuayb Al-Aqarquqy, from his maternal uncle Shuayb who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one who is hungry, so let him perform Wuzu, and let him pray two Rak’at of Salāt, then he should be saying, ‘O Lordazwj! I am hungry, so Feed me’, so he would be fed from that very moment’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ahmad from al-Hassan ibn ‘Urwah son of the sister of Shu’ayb al-‘Aqarqufiy from his maternal uncle, Shu’ayb who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘If one feels hungry he should take Wudu’ and perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer), then say, “O my Lord, I am hungry. Please feed me.” He will be fed within the same hour.’”
